title: Choose the landing structure
question: Three structural directions for the landing page. Pick one.

options.label: VU Meter Bridge
options.thesis: The landing as a row of instrument meters — each channel a feature, needles lean together on the chorus, the whole bridge reads the room at a glance.
options.viewport: Hero: a horizontal bank of VU meters where the needles all lean into yellow on scroll entrance. Each meter is a feature channel. Navigation sits above as strip labels.
options.risk: Can read decorative if the needles don't respond to real interaction.

options.label: HyperCard Stack
options.thesis: The landing as a card stack: each section a removable card with visible buttons, history trail, and the reader is also the author.
options.viewport: Hero: a single card with hand-drawn border, bold pixel-style header, and a large painted CTA button. Sections below are cards in a stack with visible link buttons between them.
options.case: Fuses with the tree-branch product truth — each card is a conversation branch, history is a trail through cards.
options.risk: Reads nostalgic for a demographic that won't recognize the reference.

options.label: Jet-Age Wallet
options.thesis: The landing as a coupon book: each leg is a feature, validation stamps mark progress, the user carries their journey.
options.viewport: Hero: a folded coupon booklet with KeyzAI as the carrier name, numbered legs (features) listed as route stops, a large CTA as the boarding pass stamp.
options.case: Strong metaphor for the journey-of-thinking product. Loses on warmth — too official for a companion tool.
options.risk: Reads like a travel agency when the ruling is too strict.
